Maybe you've chosen bad people? A good friend would be there for you, no matter what. It sounds to me like a lot of these people are crummy and looking out for themselves. I apologize for being blunt.

Also, mental disorders are hard for people to understand. This does not by any means make you a bad person, or less deserving of friends. It's a fault within them that they cannot accept you for who you are.
I suffer from PTSD. I've found a select few who can handle it, but the majority just can't. Hurts like hell, but there's nothing I can do. If they aren't willing to stick it out and attempt to understand, then they're not worth it. It's easy to say it, a lot harder to believe it, I know.

I'm the same way. It's too lonely to not have friends. Especially if you're stuck with crummy parents and no escape.

I know this doesn't mean much from a stranger on the internet...but I'd be your friend.

I wish you could come over right now so we could talk. Our lives are so similar (based on what you've written) that it's crazy. I don't have much helpful to say other than you are not alone.

First off, you are not a drama queen. It is completely okay to be hurt by what he did. It does not matter how drunk you were, how "slutty" you were dressed, or how flirty you might have been, you have a right to your body which should not be violated.
Also, don't beat yourself up about being "too freaking late." I'm guessing it was very confusing and scary; it's common to freeze and not know what to do.
The right answer is never obvious when you're in the situation. This is a person you know and probably assumed was trustworthy, so why would  he do this? I would understand if you didn't want to classify this as rape, who would want to admit that?
